newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court finds Germany late to enact environment rules.
newsitem.headline: Court finds Germany late to enact environment rules.

text.p: The European Court of Justice found on Thursday that Germany was late in enacting rules on the discharge of dangerous substances into the aquatic environment.
Germany argued the substance of the directives was effectively transposed by regulation, and a law would enter into effect in the spring of 1996.

The court reminded Germany a member state may not plead provisions, practices or circumstances existing in its internal legal system in order to justify a failure to comply with obligations and time-limits laid down in a Community directive.
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: German)
"Failure to fulfil obligations - Transposition of directives 82/176/EEC, 83/513/EEC, 84/491/EEC and 86/280/EEC on the discharge of certain dangerous substances into the aquatic environment.
Commission of the European Communities, applicant

application for a declaraton that by not adopting measures to comply with Council directives 82/176(EEC, 83/513/EEC, 84/491/EEC and 86/280/EEC on the discharge of certain dangerous substances into the aquatic environment,
and in particular with article 3 of each of those directives, the Federal Republic of Germany has failed to fulfil its obligations
1. Declares that, by not adopting within the precribed time-limits, the necessary measures to comply with
Council directives 82/176/EEC, 83/513/EEC, 84/491/EEC and 86/280/EEC on the discharge of certain dangerous substances into the aquatic environment,
and in particular with article 3 of each of those directives, the Federal Republic of Germany has failed to fulfil its obligations under those directives;
2. Orders the Federal Republic of Germany to pay the costs.
